candidate_a.apparent_claim: A masked-patch reconstruction workflow encodes visible patches, restores them to original order with learned mask tokens, decodes pixels, and applies MSE only to masked patches.
supporting_mechanisms: four visible versus sixteen original patch cells
candidate_a.paper_width_reading: All major labels readable; smallest dashed-control details are least legible.
candidate_a.prior_familiarity: Resembles a masked-autoencoder/masked-image-modeling pattern, unverified from pixels alone.

candidate_b.apparent_claim: The same broad masked-patch reconstruction workflow is shown, with a compact left-to-right forward path and a lower-right masked-only MSE panel.
supporting_mechanisms: original-target and predicted-output paths into MSE
ambiguities: exact role of yellow/white selected-location grid
candidate_b.paper_width_reading: Upper path readable; compact loss-panel labels and white selection outlines are less legible.
candidate_b.prior_familiarity: Resembles a generic masked-autoencoder/masked-image reconstruction layout, unverified from pixels alone.

comparison.shared_understanding: Both communicate masking, visible-patch encoding, reordering with learned missing tokens, lightweight pixel decoding, and a masked-only reconstruction objective.
comparison.candidate_a: Better foregrounds and preserves readability of the masked-only objective.
comparison.candidate_b: Better foregrounds a single scanable end-to-end forward pipeline and uses more recognisably image-like patch artwork.

limitations: Interpretation is confined to visible pixels and labels; diagrams cannot establish omitted operations or real-world validity.
